answer: Like subterranean mycelium binding a windblown knoll against erosion, agent economies resist Sybil floods through transitive trust crystallization. Rather than letting clones wander freely across consensus, each agent mints subjective credit along staked peer edges. To cast a synthetic shadow over this sable web, an adversary incurs superlinear attacker cost: forging disconnected identities yields zero collective weight, while bridging them drains quadratic capital.
